lead.hed: Defense News: Ulchi Freedom Shield cut to five days. A shorter drill is not a new treaty.
lead.insight: Defense News / Reuters, Wednesday: allies cut Ulchi Freedom Shield from 11 days to five — now ends Aug. 21, not Aug. 27. Seoul JCS and a Pentagon official say some field events are cancelled or moved to simulations. Kim Yo Jong called the shorter drill still provocative. A shorter calendar is not a treaty rewrite.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Army photo by Staff Sgt. Brea DuBose · DVIDS 9269296 · PUBLIC DOMAIN · UH-60 lift during Ulchi Freedom Shield 25, South Korea, Aug. 20, 2025
lead.image_note: Official U.S. Army DVIDS still from UFS 25. Not today's 2026 drill. Not a Reuters yard still. Not a brand tile. Caption must say August 2025 exercise photo, not Wednesday's cut-order.

political.hed: WORLD: Donalds takes the Florida GOP nod. Nixon takes the DSA Senate lane.
political.insight: WORLD Radio, Wednesday: Byron Donalds won the Republican primary to succeed Ron DeSantis and will face David Jolly. DSA’s Angie Nixon beat Alex Vindman for the Democratic Senate nomination and draws Ashley Moody in November. A primary tape is not a general-election map.

political.hed: Law & Liberty: a phone ban is not the same as teaching a child to read.
political.insight: Law & Liberty, Wednesday: Trepanier says screens, AI crutches, and short-passage tests gutted long-form reading. NAEP 12th-grade scores are the lowest on record. A device rule is not a book. Print first, then argue about the rest.

political.hed: Law & Liberty: school phone bans are real. Parent screen habits are the gap.
political.insight: Law & Liberty, this week: at least 35 states now limit phones in school; six added screen-time bills this spring. Hess’s point is the parent split — most still want laptops in class. A bell-to-bell rule is not a household reset.

tech.hed: Army still wants 133,000 GMLRS rockets by 2034. A paper is not a factory.
tech.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: an Army sources-sought notice asks industry how to make 133,014 GMLRS rockets by 2034 — 19,002 a year from 2028. Lockheed is already aiming at 14,000. A Sept. 1 white-paper deadline is not a signed contract.

tech.hed: DARPA’s lift contest hit 3.84-to-1. That is not four times the airframe.
tech.insight: Defense News, Tuesday: DARPA closed the Lift Challenge on Aug. 11. AVIDrone’s Katana, 29.3 pounds, carried 112.4 pounds about five nautical miles and won $1.25 million. Close is not the 4-to-1 goal. A prize flight is not a fielded cargo drone.

tech.hed: Defense News: Unitree’s robot dogs still track U.S. Army-funded research
tech.insight: Defense News, Wednesday video on Tuesday’s file: researchers say Unitree’s Go-series dogs follow Army-backed Mini Cheetah work. The Pentagon listed Unitree as a Chinese military company in June. Open papers are not a sanction. A listing is not a U.S. factory.

watch.hed: WATCH: Navy charges a Kennedy sailor in a shipmate’s death. A charge is not a verdict.
watch.insight: USNI, Wednesday: the Navy charged Aviation Boatswain’s Mate Airman Apprentice Jayjrion Rodriguez with murder, involuntary manslaughter, and assault in the death of a boatswain’s mate aboard John F. Kennedy (CVN-79). A charge sheet is not a court-martial finding.

watch.hed: WATCH: Benfold’s four-day blackout is still the readiness file.
watch.insight: USNI Monday, still moving Wednesday: USS Benfold (DDG-65) spent four days without power in the South China Sea, then left Yokosuka after a scheduled call. Underway again is not a closed engineering report.

watch.hed: WATCH: Polar Sentinel steel is up at Bollinger. Still not a delivered cutter.
watch.insight: USNI Monday from Pascagoula: stern sections of the future USCGC Polar Sentinel (WMSP-21) stand nearly four stories. Modules photographed Aug. 5. Yard steel is not ice on the bow. Pin delivery, not the class rendering.
